source_review.notes: Reviewed Treiber's report metadata and primary algorithm account, Herlihy-Wing linearizability, Herlihy wait-free synchronization, Michael hazard pointers, and current official Rust, Java, C++ draft, and Go atomic/memory-model documentation. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. Current API/order claims are source-specific and the Treiber bibliographic link is not represented as full-text review evidence by itself.

evidence: Checked abstract sequence, atomic top, immutable next relation, reachable chain, CAS expected/desired, modification order, lifecycle states, progress classes, and metrics.
Checked private, live, retired, and reclaimable node states plus operation-specific linearization events.
Checked linearizability, publication visibility, lock-freedom, wait-freedom, fairness, ABA resistance, reclamation, and performance remain distinct properties.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation connects one-word atomic transitions to whole-chain/LIFO invariants without treating address equality as object identity.

evidence: Recomputed bounded schedule: B push, retried A push, D push, and retried C pop produce four successful CAS and two failures.
Recomputed final reachable chain [1,2], popped node 3, top 1, two reachable unique nodes, and acyclicity.
Checked capacity example: two prechecks at size 99 can both admit updates, demonstrating the exact-bound race.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No contention, throughput, latency, retry distribution, allocator, or reclamation number is fabricated.

evidence: Verified successful push CAS prepends exactly one node whose next equals the compared chain; successful pop removes/returns exactly the compared top.
Verified atomic top modification order plus qualifying null reads yields a legal LIFO history under no-harmful-ABA and lifetime/publication assumptions.
Verified strong-CAS mismatch failure witnesses an intervening successful top modification, supporting system progress but not per-thread completion.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Weak-CAS spurious failures, allocation, reclamation, scheduling, and external callbacks are explicitly outside the compact lock-freedom proof unless separately justified.

evidence: Reviewed empty/one-node, push-push, pop-pop, push-pop, stale desired next, failed/spurious CAS, empty overlap, cancellation before/after point, and duplicate ownership.
Reviewed relaxed/release/acquire ordering errors, invalid failure order, ABA/address reuse, hazard publication race, epoch stall, GC/no-reuse assumptions, allocation failure, and thread exit.
Reviewed exact capacity, bulk operations, iteration/snapshot, close/drain/destruction, unbounded retries, starvation, hot-top coherence, NUMA, payload callbacks, and retired-memory pressure.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Limits cover capacity/bytes, CAS retries/backoff, allocation, hazard/epoch records, retired memory, wait/close, iteration/output, and per-thread fairness telemetry.

evidence: The model changes top only through compare_exchange, counts exact successes/failures, recomputes candidate next after interference, and preserves one finite chain.
Exact assertions check final order [1,2], pop 3, top 1, uniqueness, acyclicity, success/failure totals, and total invariant outcome.
Chapter invariants cover safe top, chain/abstract equality, private publication, protected dereference, ordering, retry recomputation, single-winner ownership, and operational policy.
invariant_checking.notes: Integer IDs are never reused and all model methods are indivisible, so ABA, use-after-free, atomics, and real memory ordering are intentionally not exercised.

evidence: Reviewed push private initialization, retry recomputation, publication, candidate cleanup, and successful-CAS point.
Reviewed pop protection/validation, null point, safe next/payload access, winner ownership, retirement, and delayed reclamation.
Reviewed LIFO history, progress boundary, weak failure, ABA trace, hazard/epoch integration, capacity/lifecycle, alternatives, evidence ladder, and all model answers.
proof_review.notes: The algorithm proof is explicitly conditional and does not silently include allocation, reclamation, exact capacity, close, or iteration in the lock-free core.

evidence: Linearizability identifies distinct success and empty points plus no-ABA/lifetime/publication assumptions.
Lock-freedom is labeled a system-wide theorem for the strong-CAS abstract core and explicitly excludes wait-freedom/fairness/bounded latency.
The finite model, history tests, memory tools, progress experiments, and benchmarks are each limited to their evidence scope.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No absence of mutexes, successful benchmark, race-tool pass, or final-state result is generalized into universal progress or memory safety.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python finite schedule model passed exact ten-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
It emits evidence=finite_treiber_cas_schedule_model and reproduces two interference failures, retries, LIFO pop, and final chain invariants.
All eight final external destinations returned HTTP 200 and all repository-local links passed chapter validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No runtime threads, real CAS, weak spurious failure, target memory ordering, arbitrary history, ABA/reclamation, allocator/cancellation, progress, capacity/close, sanitizer, or performance experiment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives Treiber transitions from the sequential stack, proves point histories and the bounded progress claim, then exposes publication, ordering, ABA, reclamation, capacity, lifecycle, evidence, and scalability obligations.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed target atomic APIs/order restrictions, private node ownership, hazard validation, epoch stalls, allocator/reclaimer boundaries, exact-capacity reservation, close/drain quiescence, bulk/iterator limits, diagnostics, fault schedules, backoff/elimination, and rollback evidence.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet supplies the core theorem and caveats; the finite schedule makes interference concrete; ten examples cover retry, winners, empty, visibility, ABA, progress, hazards, capacity, lifecycle, and benchmarking; five progressive exercises have complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Treiber, Herlihy/Wing, Herlihy, Michael, Rust, Oracle, ISO C++, Go, concurrency, security, performance, reliability, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite model prove neither a concrete runtime stack, actual threads/CAS, target memory-order choices, weak-CAS progress, arbitrary histories/schedules, ABA prevention, safe reclamation, allocator progress, exact capacity/lifecycle, fairness/starvation bounds, production latency/throughput/coherence/NUMA behavior, certification, nor deployment fitness.
